notes: This complete typed reconstruction creates two effect-specific anchor objects around the battle origin, configures both, then creates and randomizes twenty-four secondary objects before releasing the anchors.

RunBattleEffect07 and RunBattleEffect11 are 304-byte instruction/control-flow twins. Their call skeletons differ only at the two effect-specific constructor calls, and the same create/configure/release tail recurs inside the 1,264-byte RunBattleEffect05/11 owner.

Using the exact Random16 return type from the local exact-C corpus removes three spurious zero extensions and gives the readable model 296 bytes, 132 differing halfwords, and 94 wrong instructions. This is a broad source-shape baseline, not an exact-C or narrow-residual candidate, and it claims zero bytes.

Instantiating the same typed template for 0809a294 reproduces this score and residual map exactly. A joint explicit-cursor/countdown rewrite regresses both siblings identically, so the readable baseline is retained.

A bounded earliest-divergence matrix found that moving the origin declaration is byte-neutral, while block-scoped pointer/countdown loops preserve the eight-byte deficit and regress the Effect07 residual to 139 differing halfwords / 96 wrong instructions. The deficit is therefore not a simple stack-array declaration or loop-syntax artifact.

Relocation-aware six-ROM matching is ambiguous because the two sibling runners have zero-difference normalized cores. The ambiguity independently confirms the family identity but does not establish a unique per-edition owner correspondence, so no regional claim is made.
Recovered only from retained GS1 assembly, local exact-C object-update analogues, the approved compiler, and the six local GS1 editions. No GS2 evidence was used.
